title: Celeriac and apple remoulade on toast with eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or a traditional staple: eggs, celeriac, apples, Greek yoghurt, Dijon mustard, capers, walnuts and bread.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco, and celeriac is easy to find in December.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a pan, a grater, a bowl and a toaster or grill, and the techniques are basic.

works.reason: 400g celeriac and two apples dressed with 150g yoghurt and a tablespoon of mustard makes a well-balanced remoulade for four, and 8-minute eggs on two slices of toast each is a sound lunch.

honest_times.reason: Fifteen minutes is enough to peel and grate half a celeriac and two apples, peel the eggs and chop the capers and walnuts, and the 8 minutes of cooking matches the egg boil.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the lemon used for juice, appears in the steps, and the steps use nothing that isn't listed.

seasonal_feel.reason: Celeriac remoulade is a classic winter dish, it is the bulk of the plate, and serving it on hot toast suits a December lunch.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short and clear in British English, and 'remoulade' is a familiar dish name rather than restaurant jargon.

hearty_healthy.reason: Raw vegetables and fruit, eggs, yoghurt, walnuts and wholemeal toast make a filling, balanced lunch of real food.
